name: Priscillianists

citations.excerpt: This heresy originated in Spain in the fourth century
a synod was held at Saragossa in 380.

facts.value: Priscillian (died 385), Spanish theologian, later Bishop of Avila

citations.excerpt: PRISCILLIAN (d. 385), Spanish theologian and the founder of a party which, in spite of severe persecution for heresy, continued to subsist in Spain and in Gaul until after the middle of the 6th century.
Priscillian was ordained to the priesthood and appointed Bishop of Avila .

facts.value_before_verify: Priscillian (died 385), Spanish layman, later bishop of Avila

facts.value: 563, after the second synod of Braga

citations.excerpt: as an openly professed creed it wholly disappeared after the second synod of Braga in 563.

facts.value: Urged a hard asceticism, including renouncing marriage and earthly honor, alongside the Catholic faith.

citations.excerpt: he argued that to make himself a fit habitation for the divine a man must, besides holding the Catholic faith and doing works of love, renounce marriage and earthly honour, and practise a hard asceticism.

facts.value: An ascetic party. Priscillian and six companions were burned alive at Treves (Trier) in 385.

citations.excerpt: Priscillian appealed to the emperor, with the unexpected result that with six of his companions he was burned alive at Treves in 385.

facts.value_before_verify: An ascetic movement in Spain and Gaul. Priscillian and six companions were executed at Trier in 385.

research_notes: CE 1913 derives it from Gnostic-Manichaean teaching. EB1911 treats the Manichaean charge as an accusation. Neutral description avoids both.
